scope: Reviewed incremental native cage-source aperture repair for 72 fixtures, retained street stock and next-area arcade observations. Not photoreal, human, region, gameplay or V2 completion acceptance. Simplified bright glints, stretched red panels, repeated floor stock, brick relief and roof joints remain open.

images.observation: Current production approach retains regular tile courses, native timber seams and fascia stock. The former large white reflection is now a small source-sized glint. Warm cast and broader shop/detail work remain open.
Real carried light illuminates seated timber and individual grain while the smaller window glint remains. No source pose, energy, glass roughness or stock maps were changed.
Overhead decking, secondary joists and supported beams remain distinct and opaque. No native shed geometry changed in this finish pass.
Carried light shows timber direction, separate board edges and fasteners; warm production lighting remains dominant.
Separate original closure lettering remains readable on paper; seated diagonal brace and fasteners remain visible.
Closer carried-light view retains blank paper stock beneath separate lettering, board grain, joints and bolt heads.
Post/beam joint retains seated solids, end grain and bolt hardware; no new gaps through native stock.
Grazing carried light retains grain direction and bolt hardware on the unchanged native joint.

The fitted cage source produces a smaller bright glass reflection in the original camera; tile courses and fascia remain intact. The simplified reflection remains bright, without a photoreal acceptance claim.
Normal-off control preserves the small source reflection. Calibrating native source aperture, rather than changing the glass normal map, reduces the oversized oval.
Selected-material emission-off control retains the source reflection while valance darkens. Glass maps and production emission are restored after this temporary control.
Temporary right-pane-hidden control removes the remaining source glint; production pane visibility is restored. This remains a clear-window specular effect, not a wall fitting.
Front view retains original independent red lettering and softly lit fascia. Construction post partially occludes the sign; original bright projecting cabinet and period material/wording remain open.
Same front camera with only valance emission disabled: face darkens while original cabinet and practical lamp remain lit, confirming their distinct material authorities.
Left offset camera shows small finite bright source reflection through clear glazing; tile/wood stock remains readable. The lamp and glass still react to viewpoint.
Original approach camera now shows the roughly 45 mm modeled-source glint rather than the generic 160 mm source oval. No roughness or diffuse-light suppression hides it.
Right offset camera moves the reflection behind the original green mullion, retaining its correct occlusion by that frame. Lamp pose and source position remain fixed.

Native east service-lamp cage, bulb, suspension and seated bracket remain visible with real original illumination. The adjacent red panel has coarse stretched appearance and remains an open material defect.
Native west service-lamp mount is seated; source remains inside the original emitting envelope and the bulb/cage silhouette survives. Adjacent red panel finish remains unaccepted.
Close native shed lamp retains original suspension, mounting plate, cage and emitting bulb. Timber decking and joinery remain unchanged; highlights retain specular light.

Current portal observation: prior large side-glass reflection shrinks after the same native cage-family calibration. Frame, entrance floor and throat remain visible. This camera is not a region, walk or acceptance proof.
Current throat observation: brick outlines/relief, repeating floor patterns and coarse wood/cap detail need further work. Ceiling members remain visible; no structural completion is granted.

Current hall observation: native shops, open leaves, cart, fascia and roof framing remain present. Repeating floor stock, heavy brick relief and upper roof joints/openings need inspection; no region or photoreal acceptance is claimed.
